# Overview

* [Clash Royale (Windows client) — product overview](overview.md) - The Clash Royale meta-game as observed through one window on Windows — eleven screens, a scrolling bottom navigation bar, and a monetisation surface on nearly every one of them.

# Summaries

* [Clash Royale recon report, 2026-09-03](summaries/clash-royale-recon-report-2026-09-03.md) - Faithful digest of the recon report covering 11 Clash Royale screens, 43 measured screen/action pairs and 120 controls that were named but never activated.

# Entities

* [sc01 — Clash Royale main/home screen](entities/clash-royale-sc01-main-screen.md) - (screen) The game's hub screen and the most-visited screen in the model, with 20 measured elements, three exits and five currency or offer targets refused on policy.
* [sc02 — Clash Royale Battle Deck screen](entities/clash-royale-sc02-battle-deck.md) - (screen) The deck view, with 15 measured elements, Decks/Collection tabs, arrows inside the bottom nav bar, and the only measured route into the King Tower panel.
* [sc03, sc05, sc10 — the three unnamed screens](entities/clash-royale-unnamed-screens.md) - (screen-group) Three distinct screens that were each reached once, given no name or element list, and never probed — one page because there is nothing to say about any of them separately.
* [sc04 — Social screen (first of two)](entities/clash-royale-sc04-social.md) - (screen) A social screen with clan prompt, friends list, leaderboard and Quickplay, seen once, with 14 model-placed elements and no measured geometry.
* [sc06 — Social screen (second of two)](entities/clash-royale-sc06-social.md) - (screen) The other social screen, seen once, with 19 model-placed elements including left and right arrows inside the bottom navigation bar, and the only observed route home.
* [sc07 — Clash Royale Collection/Card Deck screen](entities/clash-royale-sc07-collection.md) - (screen) The card collection view, reachable only by an upward drag from the deck screen, whose entire bottom navigation bar was placed outside the window and therefore never modelled.
* [sc08 — Offers / Shop screen](entities/clash-royale-sc08-offers-shop.md) - (screen) The real-money storefront, reached by a single drag from the collection screen, carrying a €1.19 price bar and eleven refused targets — the highest-risk screen in the model.
* [sc09 — King Tower info panel](entities/clash-royale-sc09-king-tower-info.md) - (screen) A modal detail panel with measured geometry and hard stat values, where seven of eight probed inputs did nothing and its own close button was never pressed.
* [sc11 — battle result screen](entities/clash-royale-sc11-battle-result.md) - (screen) The most-visited screen in the model and the only one with no exit — sixteen distinct inputs, including its own OK button, all left it unchanged.
* [The bottom navigation bar](entities/clash-royale-bottom-navigation-bar.md) - (ui-component) The persistent tab bar at the foot of six screens — five to seven icons whose x positions differ on every screen, with scroll arrows interleaved, so no fixed coordinate addresses a given tab.
* [The top status bar](entities/clash-royale-top-bar.md) - (ui-component) The strip at y ≈ 0.03 carrying the level badge, gold and gem counters with their + buttons, and a dismissable ad icon — present on five screens, and refused on four of them.

# Concepts

* [Monetisation surfaces](concepts/clash-royale-monetisation-surfaces.md) - Where real money is reachable in this client — one €1.19 price bar, a currency + button on every screen with a status bar, three banner offers, and a whole tab — and why refusing them by coordinate did not keep the run out of the shop.
* [Panels that swallow input](concepts/clash-royale-panels-that-swallow-input.md) - Two modal panels absorbed 23 of the 24 inputs sent to them, including a confirm button pressed at its measured centre — one cause that looks identical to many independent dead controls.
* [Screen identity is a pixel measurement, not a name](concepts/clash-royale-screen-identity-by-pixels.md) - How the eleven screens were told apart — a 32x18 grid at threshold 0.94 — and the four ways that produces identities a person would not draw the same way.
* [Surfaces that are named but unmodelled](concepts/clash-royale-unmodelled-surfaces.md) - 120 identified controls were never activated, and 66 of them - the majority - were skipped for want of a decision rather than for want of permission.
* [The observed navigation map](concepts/clash-royale-navigation-map.md) - Ten screen changes across eleven screens — a graph with three dead ends, three screens nothing was seen to enter, one inescapable sink, and no route back to the frontier.
* [The saved frames do not always match the changed-cell counts](concepts/clash-royale-frames-vs-counts.md) - Hashing every before/after screenshot pair shows 7 of 43 actions report a change between two byte-identical frames — including both of the small-count transitions the model reads as panels opening.
